subject: Re: MAP — Technical evaluation plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + technical evaluation milestone (post-call recap)

Hi Elena — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and the MAP draft attached (also linked here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcDeFGhijk-ACME-MAP).

Key outcomes from today's call:
- Goal: validate Redwood as the inference platform for Acme's chat assistants (customer support + internal knowledge retrieval).
- MAP milestone we want to kick off: Technical evaluation plan (benchmarks + shortlist + success criteria).

Proposed MAP milestone (attached as acme-map-v1.xlsx):
1) Technical evaluation plan (owner: Redwood SE + Acme Eng)
   - Deliverables: benchmark spec, test corpus, model shortlist, automated perf runs, quality evals, results write-up
   - Success criteria (draft):
     * Quality: >90% acceptable responses on labeled prompt set (precision on intent classification and factuality checks)
     * Latency: E2E p50 < 150ms, p95 < 350ms for 2-turn chat (US region)
     * Cost: inference cost < $0.10 per 1k prompt tokens (target) across typical workload distribution
   - Timeline: start 6/15 — target completion 7/10; target close date for MAP: 7/15
   - Dependencies: Acme to provide redacted prompt set + representative traffic profile; procurement timeline for contract; access to test AWS/GCP project (or use Redwood hosted trial)

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm owners on Acme side for the benchmark inputs and procurement point of contact?
- If that looks right, Logan will follow up with a concrete benchmark spec and model shortlist by Monday.
- We'll update the MAP sheet and schedule a 30-min sync to finalize the test corpus.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — that looks like a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side:

- Owners: I'll own the inputs (I will coordinate with our Lead ML Eng), and Ben Cho (ben.cho@acme.com) is the procurement contact — I've cc'd him on this reply.
- The quality metric you listed makes sense; can you be more specific about the labeled prompt set size you expect and how we'll measure "acceptable"? We're concerned about sampling bias (customer support vs. internal KB use cases).
- Cost target: $0.10 per 1k prompt tokens seems aggressive for larger models. Can Logan include both an optimistic and conservative cost estimate across the model shortlist?

Also, Ben — can you share any standard contract timeline or redline expectations we should be aware of?

Elena

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + technical evaluation milestone (post-call recap)

Hi Elena — thanks for the notes. Answering your bullets and attaching a more detailed benchmark-specs.pdf. Summary below: 

- Labeled prompt set: target 1,200 prompts (600 customer support, 600 internal KB) with clear labels for intent, expected answer, and a small factuality checklist. We'll accept a bootstrapped set from Acme + augmentation from our synthetic generator if needed.
- Acceptable: we'll use a 3-point rubric for response quality (Good / Needs Edit / Unacceptable). Success = >=90% Good on the combined test set. We'll also report per-slice metrics (support vs KB).
- Cost estimates: included two projections in the attachment:
   * Conservative (larger models / higher QPS): $0.35 - $0.50 per 1k prompt tokens
   * Optimistic (quantized model variants, batching, caching): $0.08 - $0.15 per 1k prompt tokens

Model shortlist (initial):
- Llama 2-Chat 70B (int8) — strong quality, heavier footprint
- Mistral Large 22B (quantized) — good quality / cost balance
- Redwood-1.0-13B (int8) — optimized for low-latency inference on our serving runtime
- Mistral-mini / distilled ensemble (7B variants) — low-cost baseline for A/B

Latencies (preliminary targets / run-time SLA): p50 < 150ms, p95 < 350ms (US region) — these are E2E numbers including network and any small decoding overhead; we'll run real traces once we have the test corpus.

Next actions from Redwood SE:
1) Deliver detailed benchmark spec and runnable harness by 6/17 (attached).
2) Spin up a sandbox trial for Acme (hosted) or provide test creds for private deployment if you prefer.
3) Update MAP sheet with milestone owners and the target close date 7/15.

I'll wait for the labeled prompts and procurement timeline from Ben/Elena before scheduling infra runs.

Cheers,
Logan
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

Attachments: benchmark-specs.pdf
